choices: The doubly robust estimator guarantees significant improvements in statistical power irrespective of the data structure and missingness pattern.
The doubly robust approach can handle high-dimensional data and leverage auxiliary variables to potentially reduce the variance of regression coefficients under certain conditions.
If the outcome model or the propensity score model fails to be consistently estimated, the doubly robust estimator will lead to invalid inferences with inflated false discovery rates.

The doubly robust estimator's advantage persists due to its second-order adjustment for imputation errors, even if one of the nuisance parameters is only moderately well estimated under high-dimensional settings.
